chapter: On the road and into brass bands
title: First recordings in 1953 with Champion Jack Dupree and Christine Kittrell
summary: His first recording was in 1953 for King with Champion Jack Dupree, and the same year he played bass on a Nashville date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you ever do any records with him going to the studio? Did you ever...
No. I never recorded with him. Never recorded with him.
Did you do any records at Cosmo? Would you...
We did... My first recording actually was in 1953. Oh, okay. With King Records. With Champion Jack Dupree.
Uh... He recorded a song back in those days called Tied Tongue Blues. I know Tied Tongue Blues.
Yeah. I didn't know it was cut here. I didn't know it was for a new one.
It was... I know it wasn't cut here. It was cut in King. Oh, in Cincinnati.
Oh, in Cincinnati you all did it.
Yeah. You know, he did it there. But we didn't record that with him. We recorded the answer to King... ...to Song된 stuff. ...Stług된 stuff... Stług된 stuff... Stług
high blues. And that same year, I recorded with Christine Cottrell up in Nashville, Tennessee. And I'm actually playing bass on this recording of Christine Cottrell every night in the week.

Yeah. Every night in the week. I need you good loving every night in the week. A Monday night is something else. A Tuesday night is something. I recorded that with him. Damn, I can't think of the guy that recorded with him. But it was Edwin Mayer. He's playing guitar. And I can't remember who played what else. It was a young old Nat Parallel that played tennis sax. Charles Connors played drums. That was our young band. So forth.
